prompt: A transformer has 100 turns on the primary and 1000 on the secondary, with 240 V applied to the primary. Is it a step up or a step down, and what is the secondary voltage?
explanation: The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio: Vs over Vp = Ns over Np = 1000 over 100 = 10. So Vs = 240 x 10 = 2400 V. Decide step up or step down FIRST, from whether Ns exceeds Np, and three of the five options disappear before any arithmetic. Test 2 question 15 is exactly this.

why.a: Correct. Ten times the turns gives ten times the voltage.
why.b: Wrong direction. More secondary turns means MORE voltage, not less.
why.c: Wrong. That is the primary voltage unchanged.
why.d: Wrong on both direction and size.
why.e: Wrong by a factor of ten, from a turns ratio of 100.

prompt: A transformer is two coils coupled by mutual induction. Why does it work on AC but not on DC?

options.text: Because it needs a CHANGING flux to induce anything, and a steady direct current gives a steady flux
Because DC would melt the windings
Because the coils are only connected electrically on AC
Because iron cores only magnetise under AC

explanation: Faraday's law again: emf = minus N dPhi/dt, so it is the RATE OF CHANGE of flux that induces, not the flux itself. An alternating primary current makes a constantly changing flux in the core, which the secondary responds to. A steady direct current makes a steady flux, its rate of change is zero, and the secondary sees nothing at all. Note the two coils are never connected electrically in either case; the core carries the flux between them.

why.a: Correct, and it is the same sentence that governs every induction question on the paper.
why.b: Wrong. Heating is not the reason, and a transformer on DC simply does nothing.
why.c: Wrong. The coils are never electrically connected; that is the point of a transformer.
why.d: Wrong. DC certainly has a voltage.
why.e: Wrong. Iron magnetises perfectly well under DC.
